body:
From the pre-release security review of the server's network interface
(2026-07-26). Post-1.8.1.

NOTE: these two came off the review's "Minor" list and were NOT explicitly
requested — the user selected the colon and audit-trail items from that list.
Filed at low priority so they are tracked rather than lost; reject if unwanted.

## 1. app.py fails open on the dev invite HMAC key

app.py:15 defaults INVITE_HMAC_KEY to the literal "dev-invite-hmac-key", and
app.py:12 defaults SECRET_KEY to "dev-secret-key". A deployment that forgets to
set the env var starts up perfectly happily and is silently insecure: anyone who
has read this (public) repository holds the signing key and can mint valid
invite tokens for arbitrary list ids and arbitrary emails, i.e. join any list.

This IS already documented — server/README.md:148 says "Never ship the dev
default" and :149 explains the consequence. So this is a footgun, not an
undocumented hole. The argument for fixing it anyway is that it fails open: the
failure mode is silent and total, and the check is one line.

Suggested: refuse to boot when INVITE_HMAC_KEY is unset or equal to the dev
default, unless an explicit opt-out env var is set for local development. The
SECRET_KEY default matters much less — the blueprint uses no Flask sessions or
cookies (README:134 says so) — but the same treatment is cheap.

Note app.py is the dev harness, so the real question is whether operators copy
it as a deployment template. If the README's stance is that they should not,
this may be better addressed by making that stance louder instead.

## 2. No HSTS

The blueprint sets nosniff, Referrer-Policy, CSP and X-Frame-Options itself, but
not Strict-Transport-Security, so an operator who reads the "what the blueprint
handles itself" list (server/README.md:337) may reasonably assume transport
hardening is covered too.

Defensible as-is: the blueprint cannot know whether it is actually reached over
HTTPS, and emitting HSTS over plain HTTP is wrong. Options:

- leave it to the proxy but say so explicitly in the "Deployment requirements"
  list, alongside the existing mandatory-TLS bullet; or
- emit it only when request.is_secure (which requires ProxyFix to be accurate
  behind the mandatory reverse proxy — same prerequisite as the audit-trail
  ticket's source-IP item).

The documentation option is probably the right one and costs nothing.
title: deployment hardening: dev invite HMAC key fails open in app.py; no HSTS guidance
